name: Flux Factory
funding: Flux Factory received $115,000 from the New York State Council on the Arts. It bought two spaces in 2021 with funding from the City of New York.

name: New Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Contributions were $22,476,994 of $25,693,478 total revenue in fiscal year 2025. A 2016 capital campaign had raised $43 million of an $80 million goal.

name: Printed Matter, Inc.
funding: 501(c)(3) non-profit organization funded through book distribution, NY & LA Art Book Fair fees, NYSCA, NEA, and individual donors. Board leadership is closely tied to multi-billion-dollar luxury real estate development.

name: Recess
funding: Mellon Foundation (2021), Ford Foundation (2022), New York Community Trust (2023), Ruth Arts (2025). First Warhol Foundation grant in 2011.

name: Smack Mellon
funding: The New York City Department of Cultural Affairs, New York State Council on the Arts and Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts fund it.

name: Storefront for Art and Architecture
funding: 501(c)(3) non-profit organization supported by Graham Foundation, Andy Warhol Foundation, NYSCA, and individual members.

name: Triple Canopy
funding: Current institutional support: National Endowment for the Arts, New York State Council on the Arts, New York City Department of Cultural Affairs, Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts.

name: White Columns
funding: Expenses $1.3M (FY2025). NYC DCLA and NYSCA; Warhol, Frankenthaler, Speyer, Niarchos, Luce and Blavatnik Family foundations, as listed on its 2025 support page.

name: Slought
funding: Funders are listed as past: University of Pennsylvania, Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, National Endowment for the Arts, Surdna Foundation, Philadelphia Cultural Fund.

name: Artpace San Antonio
funding: National Endowment for the Arts, Linda Pace Foundation, San Antonio Department of Arts & Culture, Brown Foundation, Texas Commission on the Arts. Linda Pace Foundation gave $250,000 in 2022.

name: Southern Exposure (SoEx)
funding: Its 2021 foundation and government funders included the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, National Endowment for the Arts, California Arts Council and San Francisco Arts Commission.
